messages:
Anya K: Quick follow-up from last night's outage — we observed ~12% span loss for service:search. Root cause looks like a combination of ETL checkpoint drift (lagging job) and a recent aggregator dedupe change. Need clear owners, timelines, and monitoring changes. Who can take what?

Mike L: I can take the aggregator dedupe fix. I think we should revert the dedupe change as a mitigation. Will open INF-3381 and aim to ship a hotfix by EOD tomorrow.

Anya K: Please revert + open PR. Ping when rollback is live so we can validate counts.

Srini R: I'll own the ETL side (checkpoint drift / lagging job). Initial look: checkpoint commits are getting skipped during a rare GC spike, which causes the pipeline to skip a shard for ~30–90m. Plan: restart job, add watermark sanity checks, and add a CI smoke test that asserts steady watermarks. ETA 72 hours for full fix, will run a staging backfill tonight.

Jordan (Data Eng): I'll add monitoring and a synthetic span producer to detect sampling/producer regressions. Proposed alert: missing_spans_rate > 0.05 over 10m. Can create dashboard panels for span-insert rate, ETL lag, and aggregator dedupe counts.

Elaine: Runbook needs an update with rollback steps and rehydration playbook (how to backfill missing spans into aggregation). I will take the runbook doc and schedule a recurring postmortem review slot.

runbook-bot: Created ticket RB-4128 for runbook update and linked INF-3381, INF-3382.

Anya K: Owners: Mike=aggregator, Srini=ETL, Jordan=monitoring, Elaine=runbook/review. Please add precise due dates to the postmortem doc and create Jira tickets for any follow-ups not already captured. Also tag this "recurring-pattern" in the doc — this is the third time we've had span loss linked to ETL drift in the last 6 months.

Mike L: INF-3381: PR opened https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3381. Reverted dedupe in prod; counts returned to baseline after the revert. Running a quick canary now. :thumbsup:

Srini R: INF-3382: branch for watermark fix pushed. Running staging backfill now; if all good I'll promote to canary tomorrow. ETA ~48h for full catch-up.

Jordan (Data Eng): Dashboard updates pushed: /dashboards/spans-health. Alert rule implemented in prod: "missing_spans_rate > 0.05 for 10m" -> P2 paging to #incidents. Also added a Grafana panel for per-shard ETL lag.

Elaine: Scheduled recurring review: every Monday 11:00 for 6 weeks (first meeting next Mon). Agenda: recurring incident detection, SLO drift, postmortem action status. I'll also add a short checklist to the runbook: rollback, backfill steps, smoke test queries.

Anya K: Nice work. Quick verification checklist for owners: 1) Revert + confirm baseline (Mike) 2) Staging backfill + production catch-up (Srini) 3) Monitoring + alerting (Jordan) 4) Runbook + recurring review (Elaine). We'll consider the incident remediated when: backfill is complete, runbook is updated, and missing_spans_rate < 0.02 for 2 consecutive weeks.

Mike L: Revert done and canary looks good. I set the rollback PR description with exact steps.

Srini R: Staging backfill completed; prod backfill in progress (started 02:15 UTC). ETA for full completion ~36h.

Jordan (Data Eng): Added synthetic span producer to CI smoke jobs. Also posting the alert rule snippet for records: ```yaml
alert: MissingSpansHigh
expr: rate(span_ingest_errors[10m]) / rate(span_ingest_total[10m]) > 0.05
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Missing spans rate >5%"
```

Elaine: Runbook RB-4128 updated and linked in the postmortem doc. I've also added a short rehydration checklist for data eng to follow during backfills.

Anya K: Thanks everyone. Please mark items in the postmortem doc as "in-progress" with due dates. We'll reconvene after the prod backfill completes and again after two weeks of stable metrics. If anything regresses, escalate to P0.

Mike L: On it.

Srini R: Will update INF-3382 with backfill progress notes.

Jordan (Data Eng): Will monitor alerts and post a summary in #incidents-daily.

Elaine: Added calendar invites for the recurring reviews.

Anya K: Closing loop here — great cross-team response. Let's try to get the SLO/alert tuning + runbook done before we close this postmortem.
